title: Sanctification and the Distinction of the World
english: He has sanctified all things both divinely and carnally. Therefore, he is glorified not only in those currently possessed under his kingdom, but also in those who remained from the beginning under the kingdom; for this is the 'let your will be done on earth as in heaven' (Matt 6:10). Such also is that which is said by the angels: 'glory to God in the highest and on earth peace among men of good will' (Luke 2:14). Because of this, the Son of God came through a body, in order to extend the glory that is in heaven onto the earth, and to be glorified not only in the holy ones according to heaven, but also in those being sanctified according to the earth.

Clearly in this he divides that which is according to nature and that which is according to likeness (John 17:16); for he says that he himself is not from the world, and likewise the disciples are not from the world. It is evident, however, that Christ indeed was not from the world according to truth, until he had descended from heaven, but the apostles, according to the likeness, have descended from the world after having become like Christ. He says, moreover, that they have become men who are strangers, because of the virtue which is above man, and that they are appropriately hated by those thinking the opposite. They indeed now have with me, through the intimacy toward me, the estrangement toward the world, and no longer are bound to it. But they are anxious for the confirmation in this good thing, lest they be harmed by the evil malice of the devil and be estranged again from this divine intimacy.

Let the good be in them truly and the sanctification be real (John 17:17), lest, 'beginning in spirit, in flesh,' they should ever be accomplished, or even live according to carnal irrationality, but according to the virtue of this word, in which is again true virtue.

Much there is in this of inequality (John 17:18); for he says that he sends the disciples just as he himself is sent from the Father. There is no equality between the presence from heaven into the earth and the mission of the disciples occurring in the earth; for they are not sent as teachers by nature just as the Lord is, but having received the teaching power and wisdom, and thus through imitation, the good enters into the world, and that which was sent from heaven from the Father passes through all via the disciples sent by him.

One must pay attention to John presenting the history concerning the distress and grief of the Lord (John 18:1), which the others do not omit. But, as I have said, his writing leans more toward the manifestation of divinity, since the humanity was sufficiently foreknown; he speaks of human things more from an attack, but the proofs of divinity are clearer because of the folly.

It also seems there was a forgiveness from the Lord regarding their use of the sword then. For Luke recorded this as the Savior manifesting the impending war by saying, 'let someone sell his garment and buy a sword' (Luke 22:36), while the disciples said, 'look, two swords are here' (Luke 22:38), to which he replied, 'it is enough' (Luke 22:38). This was not a mindless thing being forgiven by the Lord, who commanded not to resist 'the evil one,' but also for the sake of what was said, so that he might show by deed what he had foretold by word, and since they were using the righteous sword, he stood and prevented them, so that they would no longer use it; as he himself, having said these things, recorded that after saying this, the Lord said, 'let it be until this,' and this 'until' has a limit and a prohibition of the use of the sword according to the law. And Luke adds to the history, 'and having touched the ear, he healed him' (Luke 22:51), which was the most manifest work toward harming no human being. But it should not be unknown that regarding such things there is also something mystical.

The cutting off of the high priest's servant's right ear should be considered by anyone as a sign of the deafness imposed upon them and of their inability to hear. For 'paralysis has come upon Israel' and 'hearing and not hearing' because of the impiety against the Savior, which was most present in the high priests. Therefore, the symbol of the removal of the ear was concerning a servant of the high priest.

And this too must be added to Luke's history, so that one might say that the restoration of the ear signifies the later restoration of the understanding of Israel, which is now removed, when they shall understand Him whom they ignored and may perhaps hear the preaching of Elijah; for the heart of the fathers shall be restored to the sons according to Malachi (Malachi 4:6). And those second ones shall be joined to us, being former according to time and...

title: The Sign of the Ear and the Timing of the Passion
english: Fathers will be numbered with sons. The cutting off of a servant-priest's ear was thus a sign of the darkness of deafness cast upon them; and regarding the restoration of the ear, one might say it signifies the later restoration of the understanding of Israel which is now spoken of, when they will understand the one they ignored and may perhaps hear the one preaching, Elijah; for then the hearts of the fathers will be restored to the sons according to Micah (Micah 7:6).

It seems John clearly intends to demonstrate what has been clearly revealed by the other evangelists regarding the day of the passion; for he has related that the supper was before the Passover feast, from which time after rising he was handed over, lest the Passover be eaten, at the very moment when the time of the slaughter of the lamb and the death of Christ was being drawn together. For the time was evening, in which 'the Spirit delivered over' (John 18:28) the true Lamb at the ninth hour of the day, and the slaughter of the lamb is also in the evening according to the law, so that by the same day and hour the event was prefigured to be fulfilled.

And the Jews were not able to escape, not that they would fulfill the event during the feast, even though they were keeping watch and saying, 'Not during the feast, lest there be a disturbance' among the people. Therefore, it is possible to understand also regarding the other evangelists that they call the first of the Unleavened Bread the one before the Unleavened Bread, that is, the thirteenth, and that a Passover was prepared for them by the disciples in this way, but the supper was not the eating of the Passover; for in this they coincide with John, and most especially the voice of Matthew coincides, whom he remembered after the Lord said: 'Know that in two days the Passover takes place, and the Son of Man is handed over to be crucified' (Matthew 26:2), as regarding this day both the Passover would be offered and he would be crucified.
He says he himself will prove the Truth to men and through his own knowledge grant salvation to them, but they stand only as far as the urgent matter.

He says that the sin of the betrayer is greater (John 19:11) because, according to the prophet, 'those whom you struck down, they themselves persecuted' and as it is elsewhere foretold concerning the betrayer, 'instead of which he did not remember to do mercy, but persecuted a man, poor and wretched, and whose heart was set on killing.' For it is a terrible thing to impose a burden of pain and tribulation in time upon one who does no wrong, instead of the righteous and good; for he to whom it was necessary to suffer, to him, having added pains, stands against God.

They lead him away as if they had conquered, but the Lord, being led, conquers, carrying upon his shoulder the beginning or the instruction, as one might interpret the prophecy of Isaiah saying, 'whose beginning was upon his shoulder' (Isaiah 53:7). It is instruction, because he bore the instruction on our behalf, according to: 'the instruction of our peace is upon him' (Isaiah 53:5); and it is the beginning, because he reigns over the captives under death and under sin, enduring on the wood the death on the wood instead of them (John 19:16). He says this forgiveness from above as glory; but he says it as a man, for according to the word, the one giving and forgiving was the Word of God and was God (John 19:16).

Many still dare to do the same as the soldiers, those scattering the church of Christ and seeking each one his own profit, doing whatever he might take (John 19:16). This was the work of the heresies of the impious. The antichrist will desire to tear apart the whole [church] just like the tunic; for indeed a people is depicted as being around the stumbling block of God, which is made manifest in those regarding Jeremiah where it was said, 'just as the girdle clings to the waist of a man, so I joined the house of Israel and all the house of Judah' (Jeremiah 3:3); but the true girdle of Christ remains, being neither torn apart nor alienated (John 19:23).

He who accepted all unmercilessness on our behalf and, drinking vinegar, says 'it is finished' (John 19:30), was demonstrating the intention of the visitation and the purpose of all things occurring therein; for on account of completion, all these things [occur], for I speak not only of the completion of the prophetic words, but also of all virtue practiced among men remaining incomplete without Christ, and of all the providence which comes from God concerning men, enjoying its completion in the salvation through Christ (John 19:30). As he breathed his last, 'the veil of the temple was torn' (John 19:30). Since it was not necessary for the harmony of the bones to be divided, this does not happen (John 19:33–34).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Side of Christ and the Resurrection
english: A side had to be struck, and this is excused for the soldiers; for the Lord provided one side instead of another. The woman's side and that which is evil from her releases the Lord from suffering; for from her side there proceeded a disastrous counsel for man. But from the holy side water and blood flow, through which the world is cleansed, having its sins removed by the joining of those who were divided according to the law; for there were blood sprinkleings for cleansing and water baptisms for purification. Since all things pertaining to Him were pre-arranged for Christ, the Lord's body provided both to the world: sacred blood and holy water, and already existing as dead according to the human manner; for it holds within itself a great power of life.

The bones of the lamb are not broken (John 19:36), showing by the type that the suffering does not belong to the power of the body; for the power of the body [is such that] our bones were being said to be [broken] by men near Hades. But that He did not die in the same way for all men, He showed the change in this, in that the harmony of His bones was not scattered.

After the Sabbath evening (John 20:1), the Lord raised the one previously foretold by Him, bypassing the three days, as it was said that the first day had suffered, but immediately the third was beginning to rise. And the three days seem to endure instead of all the time of the then-past and the then-future, delivering Himself to death instead of all those who were finishing.

Thus, rising to reach those arriving at the tomb, and no one stood by for the resurrection to be happening; for it was a mystery, if indeed something else of those administered by God, which is not manifest to men and does not lie before the eyes. A woman first stands at the tomb and at first announces to the disciples that the Lord is not in the tomb, not implying the resurrection, but thinking that He had been carried away from the tomb by the adversaries and as if calling them to a search.

After these things, seeing the Lord, she announces the blessed sight to the disciples (John 20:14). For it was necessary that the good thing be known and announced through a woman, so that the evil caused by a woman might be undone by the good knowledge which the woman brought. Not being overwhelmed by the brightness of the angels, but being surprised at the sight, she turned back and saw Jesus standing, this being the result of Him having been seen by her.

The Savior wants to show the resurrection and persuade (John 20:17), but he approaches those who have not yet heard of the resurrection in a similar way to how he approached those before the resurrection, not knowing how to fit them, unless he leads them into the same living way, so that having a familiar relationship with him, they might approach him familiarly. He says it is necessary to ascend to the Father, and after doing this second appearance, to receive the known friends and new men already approaching in the time. Do not, he says, grasp me now; for there is another great and salutary work remaining for you which I must fulfill, to ascend to the Father, who will indeed be your Father through me, and especially when I ascend the firstfruits rising from among you. This indeed she, having gone, has made good news to the brothers (John 20:19).

Falling in through the closed doors by the power of divinity, performing a transgression, he gave them the beginning to understand the power and the authority of Christ not according to the flesh nor yet according to the human manner, but beyond the nature of the flesh. And that it might be certain to appear more divine to them, it is clear from the fact that he immediately showed them only those things pertaining to the faith of the resurrection and granted the divinity of the Spirit (John 20:22). For these things were not [done] while walking with them and eating with them and resting with them and walking along with them, but he begins to accommodate himself similarly to being higher than the human way of life.

We see an inspiration in the first breathing of the soul of man being made with sanctification. For the mission was not of soul alone, even if the thing breathed in is called the spirit of life; it is clear from the prophecy of him who is immediately prophesied by the one who was breathed in; for without the divine Spirit it is not possible for prophecy to exist, as Paul testifies. Therefore, he who from the beginning breathed in, after the soul, gave the Holy Spirit himself to the soul.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
